parameters.query:
-- Claim this key, or find out who already holds it. One statement, exactly one row, no race:
-- ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE takes a row lock, so a second delivery arriving at the same instant WAITS
-- for the first to commit and then reads it, instead of also inserting. Postgres decides the winner.
-- `owner` is set on INSERT and never changed, so `owner = $2` means "this execution claimed it".
-- The no-op assignment targets `state` rather than `key` because the n8n_idem role is granted UPDATE on
-- (state, result, done_at) only: it must not be able to rewrite a key or steal a lease.
INSERT INTO idempotency_keys (key, owner)
VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET state = idempotency_keys.state
RETURNING
  CASE
    WHEN owner = $2                                         THEN 'first'
    WHEN state = 'done'                                     THEN 'replay'
    WHEN now() - claimed_at < make_interval(secs => $3::int) THEN 'in_flight'
    ELSE 'stale'
  END                                                    AS route,
  state,
  result,
  owner                                                  AS lease_owner,
  floor(extract(epoch FROM now() - claimed_at))::int      AS age_seconds;

-- Complete the lease and store what the caller should be told on every later delivery.
-- `owner = $3` and `state = 'in_progress'` keep this execution from completing a lease it does not
-- hold and from completing one twice; 0 rows back is a real condition, handled by the next node.
-- replace(): jsonb rejects a \u0000 escape (it cannot be represented in Postgres' text type), and by the
-- time this runs the work has already happened — a response carrying a NUL must not strand the key.
UPDATE idempotency_keys
SET state = 'done', result = replace($2, '\u0000', '')::jsonb, done_at = now()
WHERE key = $1 AND owner = $3 AND state = 'in_progress'
RETURNING key, state, done_at;
